British Veterans Made Some Dark Films to Protest the UK Army's Recruitment of 16-Year-Olds

I've had friends join the military right out of highschool, a lot of them having no real place to go afterwards. A good few of them dropped out pretty quickly, normal stuff. But I'd see the ones who stuck at it for three years go into their first proper tour and they'd be pitifully underprepared, more like children than soldiers.

They'd be used to their groups and surroundings like school never ended, then they'd come back from tour and you'd expect them to be made to grow up, but they come back and they haven't grown an inch in mind or body. Not until they get hurt, or lose someone. Then they grow six years in a day, worse than someone who joins the military later on. I know a good few veterans now and while most were really rattled by their time they still said they'd do it again given the same choices at the time.

The couple of kids I grew up with and did this "join at 16" thing don't say that. They don't talk about their time, they avoid questions and if pressed they just say it was a mistake joining. Now I don't have a huge sample size here, I only know about 8 people all told, but from what I've heard the 16 and up program is the shitest way to prepare new soldiers there is, it's badly designed and a lot of the reports that dictate it's funding are wildly falsified and obscured.

The fact this has gone on a few years and they still let recruiters into high schools is insane.
